objective: LINE-DETECTOR-20261023-001 proved that every two-literal tiling world contradicts along no class, one class, or every odd class (directional rigidity), and found 12 of the 30 three-place tiling placements selective, contradicting along some odd classes and not others, on every torus computed; the other 18 showed no selective pattern among eight classes. Decide whether those 18 stay rigid with more classes and larger tori, and find what separates rigid from selective contacts: an algebraic property of the pair of relations (a polymorphism, as majority closure is for two-literal contacts) or a structural one.
status: Complete 2026-10-24: which three-place contacts are rigid in direction. Polymorphisms do not decide it (all three-place contacts have trivial ones, and renaming places changes the kind); the geometry of walls does. Stripes (10 contacts) and straight walls (8) are proved rigid on every torus, with an exact count for straight walls; the 12 bending-wall contacts are selective (certified on 3 x 3, seen on every torus computed); for the 4 with no free place, a class contradicts exactly when every wall cycle collides with its own copy there. Experiment supported (26225 s against a 14400 s budget). Next recommended: walls with choices (2/3), deferred to the owner.
title: Which contacts are all or nothing in direction
